Chapter 1-Algebraic expressions.correct_answer: $$\frac{x}{x+1}+\frac{x+1}{x}=3;\ \text{Let }t=\frac{x}{x+1}\Rightarrow \frac{x+1}{x}=\frac{1}{t};\ t+\frac{1}{t}=3;\ \text{multiply by }t:\ t^2-3t+1=0;\ t=\frac{3\pm\sqrt{5}}{2};\ \text{Now }t=\frac{x}{x+1}\Rightarrow x=t(x+1)\Rightarrow x=tx+t\Rightarrow x-tx=t\Rightarrow x(1-t)=t\Rightarrow x=\frac{t}{1-t};\ \text{For }t=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}:\ 1-t=\frac{ -1-\sqrt5}{2}\Rightarrow x=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{-1-\sqrt5}=-\frac{3+\sqrt5}{1+\sqrt5}=-\frac{(3+\sqrt5)(1-\sqrt5)}{(1+\sqrt5)(1-\sqrt5)}=\frac{(3+\sqrt5)(\sqrt5-1)}{4}=\frac{2\sqrt5+2}{4}=\frac{\sqrt5+1}{2};\ \text{For }t=\frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}:\ 1-t=\frac{-1+\sqrt5}{2}\Rightarrow x=\frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{-1+\sqrt5}=-\frac{3-\sqrt5}{-1+\sqrt5}=-\frac{(3-\sqrt5)(-1-\sqrt5)}{(-1+\sqrt5)(-1-\sqrt5)}=\frac{(3-\sqrt5)(1+\sqrt5)}{4}=\frac{2\sqrt5-2}{4}=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2};\ \therefore x=\frac{\sqrt5+1}{2}\ \text{or}\ x=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}$$
